sources.entry: httpx2 - HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 client with sync and async APIs, maintained by Pydantic (httpx fork).

summary.one_liner: HTTPX2 is a Python HTTP client library with sync and async APIs, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 support, and an integrated command-line client, maintained by Pydantic as a continuation of HTTPX.
summary.what_it_does: The library lets Python code send HTTP requests through a requests-style API, using either a synchronous interface or async support. It supports HTTP/1.1 by default, with HTTP/2 available as an optional install. It can make requests directly to WSGI or ASGI applications. It ships an optional command-line client (httpx2 --help) installed via an extra. The README lists connection pooling, cookie sessions, proxy support, multipart uploads, streaming downloads, .netrc support, and strict timeouts. The project is fully type annotated and states 100% test coverage.
use_cases: make HTTP requests from Python scripts
call REST APIs with sync or async code
send requests to WSGI or ASGI apps in tests
notable: Maintained by Pydantic as a continuation of the HTTPX project under a new name
Direct WSGI and ASGI application calls
Documented Pydantic Logfire instrumentation via logfire.instrument_httpx()
caveats: HTTP/2 requires the optional httpx2[http2] extra
Command-line and SOCKS/brotli/zstd features need optional extras
Zstd decoding on Python 3.13 and below needs backports.zstd
